newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain approves Gas Natural privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Spain approves Gas Natural privatisation.

text.p: Spain approved on Friday the sale of its 3.81 percent stake in Gas Natural, the first in the five-month-old conservative government's ambitious programme of privatisation.

The stake, some 1,432,520 shares, will be sold in an institutional placement, 60 percent of which will be aimed at domestic investors, and 40 percent at international investors, state holding company SEPI said on Friday.
The sale would bring state coffers some 33.8 billion pesetas ($266 million) at Thursday's closing share price of 23,400, SEPI said.
SEPI gave no specific date for the sale, which is expected to take place in December. The sale leaves the state without a direct stake in Gas Natural.

The minority Popular Party government made clear soon after its formation that it would launch an aggressive privatisation campaign, taking up where the 13-year Socialist government it displaced had left off.
Gas Natural was seen as one of the plummest pickings.
In late September, SEPI approved the sale and in mid-October presented a detailed plan, saying the sale would take place by year-end if market conditions permitted.

Also in mid-October, the government unveiled planned 1997 sales of the state's remaining stakes in Telefonica, Repsol, and bank Argentaria as well as part of electrical group Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (Endesa).
The new government has been left with direct control over just 21 percent of Telefonica, 10 percent of Repsol, 25 percent of Argentaria, and 67 percent of Endesa.
